items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The date was supervised by Hughes Penassie and I had Herman Chittison on piano and Eugene d'Hellemes on bass.

ctx.x: But Freddy refused me because he was afraid the guitarist may come back someday for his instruments [and] although I promised that I would give the guitar back if the fellow came back and wanted it. But Freddy would not consent to my taking one, and there were four guitars in the basement going to waste! I may have been able to play guitar today if Freddy had allowed me to take one then.

January 24th 1936, I recorded for the first time under my own name. The date was supervised by Hughes Penassie and I had Herman Chittison on piano and Eugene d'Hellemes on bass. I believe it was the first jazz trip in the history of recording to be composed of trumpet, piano and bass. We recorded "What's The Reason" and "Georgia on my Mind". I had only heard Chittison play one time and that was when I first met him in 1932

in Boston. "Chit" was fast as [and] lightning and he must have heard Art Tatum many times and studied his style. He was the next thing to Art as far as technique was concerned. But he never wanted to bass to accompany him on his solos. He had a good left hand and I suppose he had the idea that the bass did not play the same pattern as he did with his left hand and it disturbed his ideas.
